results.title: Behavioral Emotion Regulation in Internalizing Disorders: A Transdiagnostic Psyc
results.reason: This study evaluates a psychometric measure specifically for behavioral emotion regulation in clinical populations with internalizing disorders, directly relevant to clinical practice for assessment and diagnosis.
results.authors: Sarah Aline Wellan; Sarah Wyka; Till Langhammer; Gina-Isabelle Henze; Lars Schulze; Lydia Fehm; Norbert Kathmann; Babette Renneberg; Shuyan Liu; Susanne Erk

results.title: Environmental Dynamics and Exam Stress among Nigerian  Adolescents: The Mitigati
results.reason: The paper focuses on exam stress among Nigerian adolescents, which is an educational/developmental psychology topic without direct clinical application for practicing therapists. While it examines stress and anxiety, the population is adolescents and the context is academic performance rather than clinical mental health interventions or psychopathology.

results.title: Motives of social media use are differentially associated with mental health out
results.reason: Study focuses on adolescents (16-17 years old) without clear adult clinical implications, and examines social media use motives rather than direct clinical interventions or assessment tools for practicing clinicians.

results.title: Effectiveness and uptake of ROOM to grow: Results of a randomized controlled tri
results.reason: This study evaluates a mobile intervention targeting emotion regulation for university students with mental health challenges, which has direct clinical relevance for mental health professionals working with young adults.
results.authors: Tajda Laure; Marilisa Boffo; Stefan Konigorski; Djameela Dulloo; Rutger Engels; Danielle Remmerswaal

results.title: Beyond Individual Resilience: Institutional Stressors, Burnout, and Coping among
results.reason: This study examines burnout, institutional stressors, and coping strategies among Baptist pastors in Ghana, which has direct clinical relevance for mental health professionals working with clergy populations. The research addresses psychopathology (burnout), mental health interventions (coping strategies), and organizational psychology factors affecting mental health.
results.authors: McFaustine Kofi Mahama; Yaw Adu-Gyamfi; Gabriel Osei Forkuo
